html:
The Koyukon are an Alaska Native people of the Koyukuk River and the middle Yukon River in interior Alaska. They speak Denaakk'e, an Athabaskan language.

For thousands of years they lived by hunting moose and caribou, trapping, and fishing for salmon in the big rivers, moving between seasonal camps. Russian traders reached the Yukon in the 1830s, bringing goods and also smallpox. In 1851 Koyukon warriors attacked the Russian post at Nulato. Missionaries, the fur trade and later the Klondike and Alaskan gold rushes brought more change. Their neighbours include the Iñupiat to the north and the Tanana to the east.
sum: The Koyukon are an Alaska Native people of the Koyukuk River and the middle Yukon River in interior Alaska. They speak Denaakk'e, an Athabaskan language.
